utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Let us review up to this point, if I may, the facts, and to portray them in the real context that they occurred, as opposed to creating history. On May 3rd, when the JNA military was attacked in the city of Sarajevo, does Dr. Stakic get up and give a speech and declare war? Does Dr. Stakic state to the citizens of Prijedor that we are at an imminent state of war, that there is an imminent threat of war? Envision this: May 3rd, Serbian soldiers from the JNA are attacked leaving the barracks in the city of Sarajevo in Bosnia and Herzegovina. On May 9th, Dr. Stakic with a purported criminal intent and a purported criminal plan speaks and gives an interview in the Kozarski Vjesnik and says that peace must be maintained at all costs. What should the inference be, that Dr. Stakic was an advocate of war, of hate, of intolerance, of an intention to destroy, as alleged by the Office of the Prosecution? What better pretext for a Serb immediately, within one week, of a gravely tragic event in Sarajevo but not to rally the troops. Instead, Dr. Stakic, as we've seen, said peace must be maintained at all costs. Keep the reality. Don't distort the facts. On May 15th, 1992, in the city of Tuzla, another attack on Serb soldiers and the JNA. What better time than on May 16th, at the 50th year anniversary jubilee for the liberation of Prijedor, other than for Dr. Stakic to give a speech and to say there was an incident at the city of Tuzla that's reported all over the news, that the Serb soldiers were Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. attacked and massacred, 150 of them, 150 injured and wounded, 300 captured? Why not at that time, if you have a criminal intent, a criminal disposition, a criminal plan, having purportedly -- or being purportedly a member of a joint criminal enterprise, why not on the 16th of May, 1992, one day after the tragedy in the city of Tuzla, does not Dr. Stakic ask of war and demand that people be destroyed or intend that people be destroyed, as alleged by the Prosecution? What does Dr. Stakic say? He tells the people of Prijedor what his goal, what his ambition, and what his intent is. He says on the 16th of May, as we previously discussed - and he's optimistic and extraordinarily hopeful - he states that "Prijedor will be an oasis of peace. Nothing ugly will happen in Prijedor." What is the inference? How do we jump, leap, even with an extraordinary imagination, to suggest that Dr. Stakic at that point in May of 1992 had the intent to destroy Croats and Muslims, was a man who deceived the Serbs, was a man who advocated war, advocated intolerance? Isn't truly objectively and intellectually it more honest to say and offer that the sole and only reasonable inference one can draw from those facts is that Dr. Stakic is not guilty of the crimes alleged, that Dr. Stakic did not possess the criminal intent necessary to commit any of those crimes, that Dr. Stakic was not aware and certainly did not know of any purported criminal plan, that Dr. Stakic indeed was not a member and participant of some joint criminal enterprise? That is not enough for the OTP. But if we ignore it, if we claim that the Defence is trying to recreate history, then maybe it will pass. The Defence is not trying to recreate history, but we want the truth to be portrayed and we want reality to be put forth before this Court and Tribunal. It's reality that Dr. Stakic in 1991, early 1992, and in mid-1992 consistently, repeatedly, and unequivocally spoke of peace and tolerance. What about the period after May 22nd, 1992? Is the inference because there are no documents, allegedly, in existence from Kozarski Vjesnik that Dr. Stakic changed his tone, changed his view, changed his opinion? One cannot draw that inference unless they are biased and prejudiced to conclude that the lack of any further newspaper articles would even remotely suggest that Dr. Stakic's intent was any different after May than what it was in May and prior to that. Whose fault is it that we don't have documents from Kozarski Vjesnik after May of 1992? Who conducted the search and seizure for those documents? Who had those documents in their possession at one time? Not Dr. Stakic. We've been adamant in requesting from the OTP those documents. They claim that at some point they didn't have a whole host of documents but upon review, re-examination, and perhaps a deep-felt examination of their conscience they decided that they had some documents that they gave us in September and October of 1992. But yet we don't have any of the documents from Kozarski Vjesnik for that critical period. Those documents were in their possession. At all times we felt and believe that those documents should have been produced. Their whole case rests on the fact that but for those documents, an inference should be drawn against Dr. Stakic. What law in any jurisdiction can they cite to support that view? But for is not the standard. The burden of proof is theirs and theirs alone to address the evidence, to assess the evidence, to argue the evidence, and to put forth the truth and to share with the Court the views when in fact there are pieces of evidence which are exculpatory and evidence and legal theories which would exonerate Dr. Stakic. Why didn't the military, as part of and member of this joint criminal enterprise, on May 22nd, 1992 not destroy the entire town of Hambarine? According to the Office of the Prosecution, there was a plan, a well-devised criminal plan dating back to 1991 that, created some sort of joint criminal enterprise, to "destroy Croats and Muslims." They needed a pretext. Forget about May 3rd in Sarajevo. Forget about Tuzla, May 15th. The Serbs in Prijedor and the military in Prijedor needed another pretext. They got one; the killing of their very own men and wounding of their soldiers on May 22nd. One would expect, and it's reasonable to infer, that if there was such a joint criminal enterprise and if there was such a criminal plan to destroy Muslims and Croatians, and if in fact there was this pretext, why stop at Hambarine? Why stop at 40 or 50 homes? Why not incarcerate and liquidate all the citizens of Hambarine? Why not go to Ljubija, its neighbouring village, where the intent to destroy Croats and Muslims was a plan, a criminal plan, part of a joint criminal enterprise? What stopped them? I'm most confused about the OTP's position and don't completely have a clear handle, if they're claiming the Muslims were armed or not armed. When we talk about legal theories and theories such as the necessity for there to be an armed conflict, they conclude no doubt there was an armed conflict. When we talk about the facts and we try to discuss who provoked whom and the ability of people who possessed arms, they take the position that there were very few arms, that there were very few -- much fewer ammunition and soldiers on one side than the other. The truth of the matter is they can't figure out which position they would like to take. If there was an armed conflict and if, as their expert Mr. Brown and Dr. Donia concede, there were paramilitary groups within Prijedor in the spring and summer of 1992, then it's plausible that there was an armed conflict. But what's not plausible is that they deny that the Green Berets existed. They deny that the Patriotic League existed. They deny that there were sales and shipments of arms to Muslims in the Prijedor municipality before, during, and after the period of the indictment. Well, they can't have it both ways. They can't say there's an armed conflict and then suggest to this Court the Muslims and the Croats had no arms to fight. The credibility of what they offer is very, very suspect, in my view. There is no doubt in Prijedor municipality in the spring and summer of 1992 there were many, many paramilitary formations and groups. Most of those groups formed, operated, and continued to exist immediately after the events of May 22nd, 1992. Pretext for the military. They only go into Hambarine. They don't go into the other villages in the Brdo region. They don't go to other towns like Ljubija. Another element they have to prove: Widespread and systematic. The Court in its 98 bis decision concluded properly that certain towns and villages, that there was inadequate proof that they were attacked, victimised, brutalised. However, the Office of the Prosecution should view that, since their indictment and their complaint says the terror, the brutality, and the "intent to destroy" was widespread and systematic. If you take anything, even a piece of paper. And if you allege for it to be widespread and systematic that it's white, and if you start to carve it out and you have only one-fourth of that paper left, hardly can you argue that it was widespread and systematic. The Prosecution did not prove that element in their case. They failed to meet the burden of proof that there was widespread and systematic conflict in the Prijedor municipality. To start, one must first examine the Prijedor municipality and take a map and highlight the areas where some of the atrocities occurred. We know that they occurred in Hambarine. We know that they occurred in Kozarac. And we know that they occurred at Stari Grad at some point on May 30th, 1992. What other parts -- or are there no other parts of the Prijedor municipality? Of course there are. That's why their theory that it was widespread and systematic does not fit and that's why the Court cannot convict, premised upon that necessary and fundamental element, that the Office of the Prosecution failed to prove. One of their experts did try to testify on widespread and systematic. And maybe I'm misquoting him by calling him an expert, but he's a journalist, and he testified in other cases as the Court has heard. He testified exactly on this issue, widespread and systematic. The Office of the Prosecution widely chose not to utilise his services on that issue for this case. Why? We saw during his testimony that he wrote articles Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. contemporaneous during the time of his visit in the municipality of Prijedor, that there was not widespread or systematic attacks upon the villages and people of Prijedor. It's in his very own articles, it's in his very own contemporaneous notes, so why bring forth the truth? Why not recreate history? Who is recreating history? If history is something that is recorded contemporaneous with the time of the events, such as Mr. Vulliamy's articles where he unequivocally says it's not widespread and it's not systematic, why not bring forth the truth. Instead, they bring him for other obvious inconsequential and irrelevant matters. Kozarac, May 24th, 1992. Presumably another pretext that the military was looking for. According to the OTP, what the military did was send the convoy through a road, the main road, knowing full well that it was going to be attacked, wanting to have that military convoy get attacked so that they can have a "pretext" to retaliate. What person, or what military soldier, would have such a far-fetched and extraordinarily imaginative plan to suggest send a convoy in the hopes that we get shot so that we can retaliate? Did the Serb military really need another pretext? They had Hambarine May 22nd; they had Tuzla May 15th; they had Sarajevo May 3rd. Why not arrest all the Muslims? Why not, if this campaign, if this joint criminal enterprise, if this criminal plan and goal was to "destroy Croats and Muslims," why not after those three significant events do you not arrest and capture all? What stopped them? We dare say that it was the voice of Dr. Stakic in the background speaking of peace, speaking of how Prijedor should be an oasis of peace, how nothing ugly would happen in Prijedor. That's not what stopped them. Perhaps it was some of the heroes that Mr. Koumjian refers to that stopped or deterred the military from attacking prior to May 24th at the village of Kozarac. Remember, Your Honours, the Office of the Prosecution at the beginning of this case told us that the JNA and, therefore, the VRS subsequent to that, Vojska Republike Srpske, was the fourth largest military in all of Europe. Can you imagine how much effort it would take if that military truly was part of a joint criminal enterprise or had a criminal plan to "destroy Croats and Muslims," what effort it would take? I suggest very little. There was no plan. There was no joint criminal enterprise whatsoever. These incidents and facts are consistent with the portrayal of reality and not the recreation of history. Reality has it that paramilitary groups were formed on all sides, the Muslim, the Serb, as well as the Croatian side. It's clear that there were sales, as we've heard from witnesses, even Serbs sold weapons to Muslims. Was there an intent by the Serbs and they're selling to the Muslims arms and ammunition? Reconcile it for me. Reconcile for me why the VRS did not on May 24th, 1992, when attacked, when its convoy was attacked, why it did not kill all the citizens of Kozarac, why it did not arrest all the citizens in the Prijedor municipality. Why did it not at that time go through all of Prijedor with the intent to destroy? It's not only illogical what the Office of the Prosecution is alleging, but it is also unreasonable. An incident occurred at Kozarac on the main road from Banja Luka to Prijedor. At that time the military responded. They responded in what their experts said justifiably. The Honourable Vassylenko asked even the Defence military expert why would the Muslims at the checkpoint, why would they provoke an incident knowing that they're outmanned, outgunned, and can never prevail? I asked that very same question with the fourth largest military in all of Europe. Why was the JNA attacked at Sarajevo? Why was the JNA attacked at Tuzla? Why were the Serb military soldiers attacked at Hambarine? Why were they attacked at Kozarac on May 24th? The will of some people, I believe, overrides the reality that they may not prevail. The Kurds in Iraq do not fear the strength and did not fear the strength of the Iraqi military. They were persistent. They continued in their belief. The Chechnyans, knowing full well that they may be outmanned, outgunned, and outmanoeuvred continued to hold strong and steadfast to that which they may have believed in or believe in. We're not here to second guess or to question why the Muslims of Prijedor shot or provoked the military. What we're here to do is to assess whether that provocation at that point resulted in a response by the military or was it as alleged by the Office of the Prosecution a pretext for the fulfilment of a criminal plan, a joint criminal enterprise, of which Dr. Stakic was part and parcel of. What an extraordinary imagination, that this plan according to the OTP, if it existed, this joint criminal enterprise, that the OTP claims existed, participants of it, such as the military they allege in the indictment, Colonel Arsic and Zeljaja, that they envisaged this plan and said, "Look, Stakic, you go out there and in 1991 you give speeches about peace. We're intending to destroy the Croats and Muslims. Go out there in January. Talk about peace. But we're intending to destroy the Muslims and the Croats in Prijedor. Set up a parallel government and tell them how you think you can work together and that you can resolve all your problems in a peaceful and civilised manner. But we want -- we have the intention to destroy them." Go to May, May 9th, at a meeting. "Tell us again, Dr. Stakic, how you want peace to be maintained at all costs. Forget about what happened at Sarajevo six days earlier on May 3rd." Participant of a joint criminal enterprise? I hardly think if Dr. Stakic was a member of any joint criminal enterprise which involved the military and six days after the tragedy at the city of Sarajevo Dr. Stakic talking about maintaining peace at all costs, the military wouldn't have responded in some way against Dr. Stakic, publicly and privately. May 16th, immediately following the Tuzla tragedy. What plan, what reasonable and logical person would think it's a plan that existed that would allow Dr. Stakic to talk about an oasis of peace and how nothing ugly would happen in Prijedor on the 16th of May? You have to have a prosecutorial extraordinary imagination. The events of Hambarine and Kozarac were certainly independent. We heard from people who were at Kozarac how well armed they were. We know from a factual basis that you do not destroy two military tanks by dropping a tree on them, rendering them incapacitated. Although, according to the Office of the Prosecution, that's a plausible and reasonable inference. They ignored their very own witnesses who told us how many people were at the checkpoints, who was armed, how many were armed, how they escaped in the woods and sheltered themselves. The military at that point, being part and parcel of a joint criminal enterprise, and having devised at some point in 1991 this criminal plan with the intent to destroy Croats and Muslims, decided two pretexts were not enough in Prijedor, the incident in Hambarine and the incident in Kozarac. So they don't kill everyone, they don't destroy everything. What they do is they start to arrest only those individuals that they feel possess a threat to them and their military so that they can interrogate them. They also tell the community that people should move away because they're going to go in there and find these perpetrators of this crime. Women and children, if there was this intent to destroy Croats and Muslims, if there was this intent to commit genocide, and if there was this complicity in genocide, which is what intent to destroy Croats and Muslims is what the Office of the Prosecution means, why spare the women and children? You have two pretexts, Hambarine and Kozarac. Your military was attacked less than two weeks ago in Sarajevo and in Tuzla. Why not kill them all? What prevented them? What was in this devious criminal plan which was part of some joint criminal enterprise that puts some limitations on the brutality and on the killings that occurred in Prijedor in 1992? Several days later, despite the fact that according to the OTP there were no arms that the Muslims had, that they were poorly armed, poorly organised, ineffective, had to use tree stumps in order to incapacitate two tanks at Mount Kozarac, or at Kozarac, nevertheless there is an attack on the city down of Prijedor. Was it organised? Was it planned? Was it criminal? Was it part of a joint criminal enterprise? On Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. behalf of whom? Against whom? At that point, the third pretext, I'm sure the attack somehow -- although I'm not as creative as the Prosecution, somehow this third attack was also orchestrated and was a pretext by the Serbs and Dr. Stakic and other members of this joint criminal enterprise so that it can be used to retaliate and to destroy Croats and Muslims. Is it reasonable to infer that at that point, ten days, three battles, May 22nd, May 24th, and May 30th, that the military at that point was truly, solely, and exclusively conducting all operations in Prijedor? That no one at that point was even remotely visible to give interviews or to discuss facts or to hold any types of meetings? Is it not reasonable that at that point the third so-called pretext by the Serbs necessary in order for them to fulfil their criminal plan and joint criminal enterprise, that at that point why didn't they go into Brdo region? Why didn't they on May 3rd with the intent to destroy all Croats and Muslims in the community, why did they stop at Stari Grad, where the attackers of the city town of Prijedor decided to retreat at? Why not just go several kilometres and arrest everyone in the Brdo region? What kind of a plan was it, a plan that dictated that two and a half months later, on July 20th, 1992, the military would come back and start to arrest civilians, unarmed? They wait six weeks in order to fulfil their plan when they're immediately at Brdo on May 30th, they're in Brdo on May 22nd, yet this intent to destroy was somehow derailed or delayed for whatever reason? There's no logic. There's no reasonableness. There's no truth to the allegations offered by the Office of the Prosecution. These were regrettably not pretexts. These were regrettably true and accurate events that occurred in Prijedor, in Sarajevo, and in Tuzla. These were facts that were not created by the Serbs or the Serb military to be used as a pretext so that they could fulfil and attain their goal of destroying Croats and Muslims. The fourth largest army. The Muslims were unarmed, lack of ammunition, lack of resources. They needed no time, no pretext, and no plan in order to systematically destroy them, if that was the plan, the goal. I tell you that there is an attack on all the Serbs and not just Dr. Stakic. I think it's a reasonable inference that when a Serb such as Dr. Stakic talks about peace, when a Serb such as Dr. Stakic maintains peace and order will prevail throughout a most critical period, that it must be a pretext, that it must be an attempt by the Office of the Prosecution to muddy the Serbs as well as Dr. Stakic. Have you once heard the Office of the Prosecution in their analysis and assessment try to share with you how is it remotely possible that other parts of the Prijedor municipality were untouched, that other Croats, namely in Ljubija, were unharmed yet this was this plan intentionally to destroy Croats and Muslims? Is the plan to intentionally destroy only the Croats and Muslims in Hambarine on May 22nd? Did they really have this preconceived and premeditated, as they call, plan to perpetrate a crime at Kozarac and therefore kill several Muslims, detain hundreds and thousands of them? Was that their plan? Their plan, according to the Office of the Prosecution was, "To intend to destroy Croats and Muslims." All of them, not one according to this criminal plan and this joint criminal enterprise was expected to survive. I submit to you the reasonable inference, looking at any of the demographic figure, even those offered by Dr. Tabeau, which I suggest to the Court and which I'm confident the Court agrees are not valid, should not be given any weight, but those figures or the supporting documentation that she does use does reveal one fact and an extraordinary fact, that there was no criminal plan, that there was no joint criminal enterprise, that Dr. Stakic is not culpable directly or as an accomplice to any of the tragedy that occurred in the spring and summer of 1992 in the Prijedor municipality. I believe, Your Honour, this might be an appropriate time. I might move to another area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Please be seated. Before I give the floor once again to the Defence, may I announce that we start tomorrow 9.30 in Courtroom II with a Status Conference, and then let us hear the closing arguments in rebuttal and rejoinder, followed by a limited line of questions by the Judges, and then finally Dr. Stakic enjoys the right to have the last word. In the afternoon we will proceed in Courtroom III because Courtroom I is occupied for the purpose of an initial appearance in another case. Anything else in the moment? It's not the case. Then please, Mr. Ostojic, proceed with the third part of your closing arguments.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and good afternoon. Your Honour, this morning, we attempted to reveal for the Court what we believe the true evidence and the inferences from that evidence in reality are. When you look at the magnitude and scope of the evidence presented by the Office of the Prosecution, we find very little in terms of the circumstantial evidence that would lead to a conviction of Dr. Stakic for any of the crimes that are alleged against him. We insist, and the law requires, that the Office of the Prosecution meet their burden of proof, a burden of proof that I concede is extremely high, but a burden of proof that is set by the criminal law system of this Tribunal and other jurisdictions throughout the world: Beyond a reasonable doubt. Never were those words uttered by the Office of the Prosecution. Never have they suggested or told this Court that the evidence that they claim to have satisfies or meets the burden of proof beyond a reasonable doubt. This Court as well as the Office of the Prosecution and the Defence attorneys recognise that a circumstantial case is difficult. It's rendered more complex because of the inferences that must be drawn related to the evidence, both documentary, extrinsic, and from the lay witnesses that are brought before the Court. It is made more complex because there are presumptions that one can make as to each of the facts if there is no direct evidence to the contrary. What we suggest and what we state to the Court without any reservation is that the evidence is compelling that Dr. Stakic is innocent of the crimes alleged in the fourth amended indictment. The OTP tries in vain to argue many facts as they have throughout this one-year long trial. The Court in its wisdom restricted them on numerous occasions when they discussed things like Dr. Stakic's brother. Why did the OTP necessarily care or wish or desire to raise that issue? To muddy the waters. To dirty the playing field. To throw mud unnecessarily on Dr. Stakic. Interestingly enough, with respect to Dr. Stakic's brother, the OTP at all times knew that that which they were proffering was inaccurate and untrue. They don't stop there. Next, they try to argue, although with their consent, we tried to confine the parametres of this case to the indictment period, 30th of April through the 30th of September, 1992. Nevertheless, they argued that flight should be considered an important topic and issue. The purported flight of Dr. Stakic. The Court in its wisdom reasonably restricted and ordered that they refrain from bringing such issues and such tactics before the Tribunal. The indictment as we have alleged, as is evident simply by taking judicial notice of when the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: -- And when he was initially and ultimately arrested and incarcerated. The OTP, however, does not stop in its efforts to muddy the waters, but they now do it in a more subtle way, in a bit more of a clever manner. They are not as direct because of the Court's stern warnings. They are not as aggressive in their tactic, however they persist ever so tirelessly to muddy the waters and to try to dirty Dr. Stakic. utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll do so. The Office of the Prosecution does not discuss the law because the law, if applied fairly, objectively, and honestly, does not assist them in the application of the facts. The only reasonable inference from the circumstantial evidence and the presumption of innocence is that this Court must acquit Dr. Stakic. How has the OTP been subtle in raising things such as innuendo or items that are somewhat irrelevant and immaterial to this case. On one hand, whenever Dr. Stakic attempted to do something, the Office of the Prosecution in all their wisdom claimed that it was an aggressive act, that it was part of a plan -- part of a criminal plan, part of a joint criminal enterprise. They raise the issue of curfew and disarming members of a society. They claim -- and that's the only piece of evidence that they put forth that they allege came from the ARK from Banja Luka. They claim that disarming citizens during a heightened state of tension is wrong and is criminal. In fact, they go well beyond the line of reason. They state in their closing argument, page 42, line 21: "As in most genocides, the first thing you do is ask the victims to please disarm. On the order of the authorities, disarm." Wow. What an extraordinary imagination. So put down your arms is the first step in most genocides? I honestly don't know what to say. I honestly am speechless when I hear those words and that tactic uttered. But I do have a proposition for the Office of the Prosecution. Perhaps the Madam Prosecutor next time she visits the United Nations at the Security Council, she can share with them the Prosecution's view that as in most genocides, the first thing that happens is a request to disarm. Share that view with the Security Council. In fact, when Madam Prosecutor shares that view, she should bring with her Security Council resolution number 752 dated May 15th, 1992, involving specifically Bosnia and Herzegovina where the Security Council themselves in a unanimous decision on paragraph 5 -- I can have it if the Court would allow for the usher to please place it on the ELMO. This document, and the Court can take judicial notice of it pursuant to the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal, with respect to this document involving Bosnia and Herzegovina May 15th, 1992, within the period of the indictment involving the territory that's at issue, at that time, the Security Council with all its wisdom certainly didn't buy into the Prosecution's rather broad and general attempt to muddy the waters by suggesting as in most genocides, the first thing that happens is a call or a request for the victims to disarm. Paragraph 5 states, I believe it's clear although I'm reading from my notes: "Demands further that all irregular forces in Bosnia and Herzegovina be disbanded and disarmed." Is really disarming the first step to genocide as the OTP alleges and claims? If the Court looks at the date of that resolution and matches it with the date of documents which call for disarming, he'll find that it was consistent with what the Security Council felt was appropriate, not appropriate to start genocide, not appropriate to victimise innocent citizens, but appropriate to calm tensions, appropriate to remove future tensions and provocations, appropriate as an attempt at peace, not genocide. What can we infer from the comments suggested by the Prosecution, that Dr. Stakic's alleges call to disarm was his first step to a plan, a criminal plan, a joint criminal enterprise to destroy Croats and Muslims? What was the intent of the Security Council Resolution 752? I hope that the Office of the Prosecution doesn't suggest that the Security Council asked people to disarm because that was the first step to genocide, or in their fanciful imagination, are they, too, part of this wide and broad joint criminal enterprise. In their fanciful extraordinary imagination, could it be possible that their inference is not only illogical and unreasonable but completely distorted and untrue? Quite frankly, I don't mind aggressive advocacy. However, advocacy which distorts purposefully facts and which tries unnecessarily to obtain advantage are absolutely prohibited and should not be allowed. The Office of the Prosecution next discusses magnitude of killings. They don't give the Court an honest view of that. They don't share with the Court the military reports which clearly and unequivocally cite that the killings in the Prijedor Municipality were random, sporadic, and uncontrollable. They don't give their military expert or consultant all the evidence so that he could reach a reasonable conclusion based on the military reports that were made contemporaneous with the events in the spring and summer of 1992, that there is no doubt, and if any doubt, little doubt, that the crimes that were committed were indeed sporadic, random, and uncontrollable. That would certainly fly against their broad theory that Dr. Stakic had a plan, that Dr. Stakic was part of a plan, a criminal plan, a joint criminal enterprise. When they discuss joint criminal enterprise and the purported participants in their fourth amended indictment, the Court will find that they list few and give us the legal "among others." Who are they? We're here for the truth. We know it's not the Security Council, although based on the Prosecution's evidence perhaps I'm not so sure. We know that their theory is overly broad and inconsistent with the evidence. We know that of the participants that they identified as coconspirators in this joint criminal enterprise, none of their documents were produced to us. None of the documents from General Talic, Radovan Karadzic, Biljana Plavsic, Arsic, Zeljaja, even Simo Drljaca, even the late Dr. Milan Kovacevic, none of their Rule 68 documents were ever produced to the Defence. Why? What is the inference? The inference must be that there is a lot of evidence against these individuals, that's why they didn't bring it in. They didn't want to dirty our case. They didn't want to have too much evidence against Dr. Stakic. Or in reality, is the evidence that if this Court and if this Tribunal had collectively all the evidence of these purported joint criminal enterprise perpetrators, that it would be little, there would be little doubt that Dr. Stakic would be found innocent of the crimes alleged? Magnitude of the killings. I suggest to the Court and Your Honours that when viewing the magnitude of killings and their argument on that, look for things like where, when, and over what period of time did these atrocious acts take place? Do not accept their view and some computer-generated chart which suggests that in May of 1992, 112 Bosnian Muslims and Croats died. It's impossible based on the evidence. Imagine this: Three attacks in May. May 22nd, the military with an intent to destroy, with the pretext, attacks Hambarine. Several days later, the military with a pretext attacks Kozarac. And according to the Prosecution, they were preplanned and premeditated. They had a wonderful formation, typical military formation. And then several days later, they bombard Stari Grad after an attack on the city/town of Prijedor, May 30th, 1992. If there was a campaign to destroy Croats and Muslims, having three pretexts in May, wouldn't they, the army, military, these coconspirators, those people who were so well armed against the unarmed civilians, wouldn't they have been able to implement and complete their plan and kill more than 112? We're going to ask the usher, with the Court's permission, to place S281-3 on the ELMO, please. Thank you. Now, the OTP relies on yet another in-house expert or consultant. I forget how he likes to be referred to. Mr. Nicolas Sebire. And this is his exhibit, S281-3. And I believe the Court can see that in fact based upon Mr. Sebire's analysis and his thorough and objective review that in May 1992, 112 Bosnian Muslims and Croats were killed. Three attacks, a criminal plan, a plan to destroy the Croats and the Muslims, and they kill only 112 in a critical month where the Prosecution claims was a pretext. You know what I think this graph is, I think this graph is a fraud, and I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. think this graph is a pretext to an argument that the Office of the Prosecution had at one point. Their argument at one time was "let's see if we could fit all the crimes during the period of time that the Crisis Staff was in existence." May 20th through July 24th, 1992. That's why Nicolas Sebire assists the Prosecution and says "that's easy. We have the sophistication, we have the knowledge, the lack of integrity, and we will put all of the deaths or most of the deaths within those three months. So we will shift all the blame on the Crisis Staff." The OTP states with confidence that from Mr. Sebire's report and his database of 900 or so deaths "we see that the crimes escalated, reached their peak in July, but May, June, July, and August, and then last for August, the reason that that happened is the visit of the journalists. When the eyes of the world focussed on Prijedor, the genocide could no longer be carried out." Is Mr. Sebire really a witness that the Court should give any weight to? Is he credible based on this graph that they rely on so convincingly and with such confidence in their closing argument? What Mr. Sebire forgot to do was to check and see if their strategy and tactics changed. What Mr. Sebire forgot to do was to read the fourth amended indictment. Let's take a look at August. I know I'm not a mathematician or a statitician or perhaps I can't read very well, but I think I can decipher the facts that Mr. Sebire and the Office of the Prosecution are simply distorting the facts before this Tribunal. August of 1992. What's their position? It all depends what you read. It's a moving target. If you read the fourth amended complaint, on August 5th, 1992, 120 Bosnian Muslim and Croats were liquidated and killed. 120. They have alleged it. They have even said it in their closing argument. Let's look at what Mr. Sebire says in his graph which was purportedly objective. He says 108. I've never studied addition by subtraction, but Sebire certainly should have known by reviewing the fourth amended indictment that something is wrong with his graph. Something is wrong. What's wrong with it is this graph was a graph that was used in another case, I suggest, that seems to indicate "let's put all the crimes during the period that the Crisis Staff was in existence." Is it true what the Office of the Prosecution suggests when they tell us about this exhibit S281-3, that: "The reason that there was fewer crimes and killings in August was because of the visit of the journalists. When the eyes of the world focussed on Prijedor, the genocide could no longer be carried out." 120 on August 5th, 1992. We can say that it's a small amount, and if we have a margin of error, which Dr. Tabeau doesn't understand, but I'm confident that most of us do. If we have a margin of error, it's close, 120, 108. How credible is his report when in the indictment the Prosecution says that 200 Bosnian Muslims and Croats were executed at Mount Vlasic, their graves exhumed with the participation and assistance of Mr. Sebire. Is there any doubt that unforeseen -- unforeseeable criminal act happened on August 20th, 1992? How does Mr. Sebire come up with the analysis after reading the fourth amended complaint, indictment, participating in the exhumation, reviewing the evidence in this case? How does he come up with the 108? His evidence in whole is not credible. Their charts and their graphs in whole should be rejected and dismissed. None of the evidence offered by their experts in my view are deemed reliable. But all it was was a sophisticated, computer-generated support for the Office of the Prosecution and their "whenever and whatever" theory of the case. The Defence has tried with some restraint to present a balanced approach, to present evidence that is indeed objective, evidence that indeed comes close to the truth, to the best of the recollection of the individuals who live there. The Prosecution makes some argument about the late Dr. Eso Sadikovic and how if he were given an opportunity to speak at one of the detention centres in August of 1995, how the world would have known what was going on. Needless to say -- 1992, sorry, obviously. I want to get to another subject that covers 1995, so I'm ahead of myself. When he mentions the late Dr. Sadikovic, he mentions that he's a good man, he mentions that he's an honest man, that he's a peacemaker. He mentions also somewhat shockingly that he's married to a Serb. What difference does it make? What difference did it make? Is it true that they're now striking at our emotional strings and at our hearts? When the Defence brought what we considered a balanced view of Muslims, of Croats, of Serbs, of other non-Muslims and non-Serbs to testify, one of their first, and I must say consistent questions, who are you married to? Who is your brother-in-law? Do you have any Serb blood in your family? Is that in an attempt to increase the weight that should be given that witness? Or is that a subtle attempt to signal the Court "he's part Serb, dismiss his testimony as a whole"? Yet, on the other hand, when the late Dr. Sadikovic is discussed, it's a badge of honour to say that he was married to a Serb. What they're trying to do, as I stated this morning, is to have a double standard. Their graphs are inappropriate, should be rejected. Their arguments when honestly and objectively analysed, such as as in most genocides, the first thing is to disarm, are truly, truly inappropriate and do not have any basis in either law or fact. We talked a little bit about their evidence and what they're relying on and how they have weaved the fact that Dr. Stakic in 1991 became vice-president. Forget about that he spoke of peace. In January of 1992 when the parallel government was established, forget about that it was public, ignore the fact that he spoke about peace at that time as well. Don't allow yourself to know or learn that on May 9th, Dr. Stakic spoke of peace publicly, openly, consistently. One week later on May 16th, he did the same in a public forum. They don't even address our evidence. D99, if that can be placed on the ELMO. They talk about some link between Dr. Stakic and the police because their case has been -- excuse me. If you can just hold on. Their case has been rendered or has been reduced simply to blaming everything on the police and simply trying to use broad baseless unfounded arguments to connect and establish a link between the police and Dr. Stakic. Why do they go painstakingly through Kozarski Vjesnik to find even the slightest negative quote that Dr. Stakic may have made. Why don't they fulfill their duty and obligation and say, We will put forth to the Court the truth and show the Court if other purported coconspirators in this joint criminal enterprise, if they said something to exonerate Dr. Stakic during their interviews and the civilian authorities. That's not their mandate. That's not their job. Their job is to convict at all costs. Their experts prove that. Their graphs prove it. Their arguments certainly prove it. Kozarski Vjesnik, the 9th of April, 1993, an interview with Simo Drljaca, if it can be please placed on the ELMO, first the first page that we can that. It's marked as D99. The Court will remember the argument that was raised by the Office of the Prosecution. It's outside the time period of the indictment. It's irrelevant. They used that argument consistently when there's any evidence to exonerate Dr. Stakic. Page 2 of that article clearly states within one year, not two years later like some interviews we heard Dr. Stakic gave, within a year of the tragic events in the spring and summer of 1992 in Prijedor, Simo Drljaca states unequivocally, and it's in the last paragraph, second sentence -- third sentence: "After the takeover of authority, however, the new people did not understand the real role of the police. The attempt to transform the police into a council body which would execute orders given by the council civilian authorities was unacceptable and misunderstandings arose." Simo Drljaca April 1993 states that the civilian authorities wanted to obtain some sort of relationship so that the police would execute their orders, but he says "it was unacceptable because" and the only reasonable inference we can draw from that comment is that there was no one who was superior to Simo Drljaca in Prijedor in 1992. How could they reconcile this? Did other witnesses perhaps talk or share with us misunderstandings that arose between Mr. Drljaca and the civilian authorities? Ignore it. It doesn't fit their case. Ignore it because if you accept that evidence which is verified by Mr. Drljaca himself, then it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. would create a reasonable doubt, and the Prosecution would fail in meeting their burden of proof. How can we reconcile these issues, the only honest way and the only objective way to reconcile them is in favour of Dr. Stakic. The only reasonable inference from the evidence is that Dr. Stakic is innocent. The only reasonable inference from the circumstantial evidence that even the Prosecution brings forth is that Dr. Stakic should be acquitted. The only reasonable inference is that Dr. Stakic was at no time a participant in a purported joint criminal enterprise. At no time did Dr. Stakic possess or have any criminal mens rea or intent against the Bosnian Muslims or Croats in Prijedor. Let's take it one step further: Let's assume that the Office of the Prosecution has a duty and an obligation to put forth evidence in an honest, objective, and truthful manner. Why not give this statement that Drljaca gave to the military expert? Let's see what he would think about it or opine about it. Why not get their in-house personnel, their police officers who do a masterful job of search and seizures and following the rules of chain of command, why not have them interpret or opine what that statement means? The presumption of innocence is with Dr. Stakic. The inference as to their lack of presentation of police experts and lack of presentation that anyone evaluates or analyses these documents, the inference is that Dr. Stakic is not liable for any of these crimes, is not culpable for the atrocity that happened in Prijedor. We can go one step further in a logical manner and say we looked at the evidence as to what type of person Mr. Drljaca was. We brought evidence in connection with that; the Office of the Prosecution didn't. It never argued Mr. Drljaca was a man who followed authority, respected authority, knew when not to cross the line with any authority, civilian, military, or police. What happened in 1997? What happened to Mr. Drljaca in 1997 is consistent with Mr. Drljaca's unfortunate character, personality, and reputation. When he was shot and killed, he again did not stop for the authorities. He did not in 1997. He certainly in 1992 would never have allowed himself, as he so says, to fall under or to be subordinate to the civilian authorities in Prijedor. The inference clear as day is that there is no link between the police and Dr. Stakic, between the police and the political civilian authorities. However, if we're blinded by emotional tactics, blinded by someone pulling at our heart strings, we will ignore all that evidence. We will certainly not view that evidence objectively and pursuant to the law. Now we're discussing Mr. Drljaca, and if the Court remembers, on the 23rd of March, 2003, there was another brief exchange between the parties. And the Defence sought to present to the Court their 65 ter number 584, which discusses and is a document from 1994. The Prosecution in its fairness, in reaching its mandate, they object and they state: "It's not relevant. The indictment -- it's not relevant to the indictment. It's a 1994 document." The Court unfortunately stated: "After deliberations, dismissed as not relevant." How is the fact that the Office of the Prosecution can sit here and tell us last Friday that Simo Drljaca was brought back to Prijedor hand in hand with Dr. Stakic in 1996 when the evidence that the Defence is trying to prove and in fact established that in 1994, Simo Drljaca was already placed in and was the chief of police in Prijedor, two years before Dr. Stakic returned? But according to Ms. Sutherland, when she shares with the Court, she says it's not relevant to the indictment. It's a 1994 document. I would think that if it's not relevant, they should stand on that position. I was rather surprised to have them now discuss that bringing in 1996 purportedly Mr. Drljaca with Dr. Stakic back in the municipality of Prijedor is an element or a factor that this Court should consider. Double standard? Of course not. It's okay if they talk about 1996. Talk about it honestly. Tell the Court honestly when Mr. Drljaca became the police chief in the Prijedor Municipality. Don't cloud the issues. Don't muddy the waters. It's unfair, it results in a travesty of justice. It honestly shocks the conscience when you review arguments such as those made by the Office of the Prosecutor, when they're restrained from discussing Dr. Stakic's brother, when they're restrained from a baseless and unfounded allegation of flight, and yet in a subtle way, less than one month ago, they say that the document that shows Simo Drljaca was the police chief in Prijedor in 1994, it's not relevant to the indictment, but then they come into Court and they tell us that they came hand in hand. As the late Professor Cehajic said and as Dr. Stakic always maintained, the truth will come out and justice will prevail so long as we analyse critically and objectively each of the arguments, each of the allegations and assertions made by the Office of the Prosecution. We cannot and most respectfully to the citizens of Prijedor, particularly those victims who are Bosniaks and Croats, but we cannot view this case from the end result and to try to show justification and to shift blame for the atrocities that they have suffered and continue to suffer. We cannot allow the justice system to be the avenue in which blame unjustly and unfairly would be shifted to an individual. Certainly the witnesses that we heard, listened to, discussed, not one of them, including the honourable Dr. Minka Cehajic, who was extremely, extremely passionate when she testified, one of the persons who we would expect as a reason to blame, a reason to find guilt with others, her husband being the past -- the predecessor of Dr. Stakic, the president of the Municipal Assembly, she could have easily said if she believed in her heart that Dr. Stakic was guilty, she would have and she could have. But she didn't. Why? Why didn't Dr. Minka Cehajic say that Dr. Stakic is responsible? Why didn't Dr. Minka Cehajic say that Dr. Stakic should be given a life sentence for the crimes that occurred in the Prijedor Municipality? Is it because she knew Dr. Stakic? Knew him well? Liked Dr. Stakic? Liked him well? Of course not. The only reasonable inference we can draw from her testimony is that being a well-educated, a well-informed individual, knowing that her husband, her late husband, Professor Muhamed Cehajic, held the same position as Dr. Stakic, she knew and knows today that Dr. Stakic at that time was indeed powerless and had no authority over the sporadic, random, and uncontrollable criminal acts and killings that occurred. We obviously thank all the witnesses who participated in this trial. We know it was very difficult for them, and we know that they continue to suffer. Our deepest sympathies go out to them as they have from the outset. We acknowledge and appreciate the courage that they have and had to participate in what they deem to be in which I still believe is a fair and just system, despite the Office of the Prosecution's tactics. Now, the Office of the Prosecution decides in a subtle way, of course, that it's not enough because we don't have enough evidence, so we must continue to muddy the waters. And let's pull out some quotes from Dr. Stakic that he talks about the jihad, that he talked about Islam and how that is offensive and how that is wrong and how that in some manner equates to criminality. But what the Office of the Prosecution doesn't want to focus on, when were those comments made? Do we have any evidence that Dr. Stakic made those comments before or during the period of the indictment? What we do have and what this Court can take judicial notice of are two, at least two, public indictments against Sefer Halilovic and Mehmed Alagic under IT-01-48 and IT-01-47. Why is that significant? Well, in the OTP's indictment, although they find the mention of jihad repulsive and criminal, they state: "The mujahedin who principally came from Islam, from Islamic countries, began to arrive in Bosnia and Herzegovina sometime during the middle of 1992." The Office of the Prosecution continues to state: "They were prepared, the mujahedin who came from the Islamic countries in 1992, they were prepared to conduct a `jihad' or `holy war' against the enemies of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Muslims." The Office of the Prosecution makes that allegation against the Muslims. If it's mentioned by a Serb, it is criminal. The Office of the Prosecution does have a double standard. The fact that in 1994 and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. sometime later, Dr. Stakic made what would be considered impolite, wrong, inaccurate comments should not have even been allowed in this case, should not have been permitted to be brought forth if we have a fair system and if, according to the Prosecution on the 23rd of March, 2003, it's irrelevant because it's outside the period of the indictment. It's 1994. The fact that evidence that the Defence would like to put forth regarding Simo Drljaca in 1994 is not relevant. It becomes relevant when bald-faced, unfounded allegations are made relating to 1996. It becomes relevant when they're given the opportunity unilaterally to discuss interviews of Dr. Stakic of 1994. They talk about jihad and the holy war. They mention it in their public pleadings. What expert were we able to convince or to help us understand whether there were paramilitary units in Bosnia and Herzegovina and in Prijedor in mid-1992? Every time we mentioned the Green Berets or the Patriotic League or other paramilitary formations such as Ramsay's group, we were confined, restricted, and asked to move on. The Office of the Prosecution in their attempt to be objective calls their experts and, as I've stated earlier, only haphazardly give them documents to review. What about D12? Probably everybody's thinking "what about it?" D12 I think is an important document. It's a document that the Office of the Prosecution always had, continued to have in their possession, but refused intentionally to give it to their experts, their military expert, their police experts, their computer experts, or any of the multiple in-house consultants that they have at their fingertips. Why is D12 so important? If the assistance of the Court the usher may be permitted to place the document on the ELMO. It is a military report that was compiled on the 17th of November, 1993. It's a military report of some significance because it shows and helps us understand the conflict as it may have existed, but that's something that we don't necessarily want because it might detract from the theory, from the goal, from the mandate of the Office of the Prosecution. And that is they're looking for a conviction at all costs. I would think that if I were to hire a military expert or use one in-house, I would tell him to be cautious of this document and to somehow in their creative way come up with an argument to distort, as they have the other evidence, or to dismiss the factual basis within that document. It is an enormously lengthy document prepared with an incredible amount of detail. In fact, when given the opportunity, there is no doubt that the Office of the Prosecution knows in their hearts that this document is fair and is honest. They themselves on page 2 of that document, if I may, on the top portion of that document, the Court will see is a note from an employee from the Office of the Prosecution. That note, after someone reviewed the document, tells us in essence "the statement seems unbiased" on the fourth line down, "and is equally critical of Muslims and Serbs." In the possession of the Office of the Prosecution, they have evidence that their own staff, their own personnel, conclude that it's unbiased, critical of both, yet do they ever give it to any of their experts? Yes, they should, if their mandate was to have a fair trial, if their mandate was to show the Court what the truth was. Instead, they recreate evidence, manipulate facts, and distort the reality before this Court. What is the inference we should obtain or draw from the fact that this document was never utilised by any of their experts? Another mistake. Another omission. We know this Court has been enormously generous with both sides in giving us ample opportunity to present evidence. In fact, when it came to the prosecutorial experts, they were given numerous occasions to recreate, redraft many of their computer-generated data, graphs, and figures. Why wouldn't their expert, why wouldn't the Office of the Prosecution, knowing what the mandate is of this Tribunal, simply give this document in excess of 300 pages to their expert and tell him "review it" -- strike that, in excess of 220 pages, "review this document, D12, how would it impact your testimony, how would it change any of your opinions?" We know what the answer is, but pacify us, indulge us. The answer that Mr. Brown and every one of those experts would give is that it doesn't affect my opinion. It wouldn't change my analysis. It simply is a non sequitur. But then we can judge -- the Court can judge and assess in reality what weight to give those experts, what weight to give the credibility of the statements that they offer here. Why wouldn't the Office of the Prosecution contact their expert and say, "Here's an exhibit you haven't reviewed. Let's do the right thing. Let's do the honest thing. Let's have you review it, and we'll make an application to this Court that you reviewed it and would like to submit a supplemental opinion and report." Thank you. Next topic -- would we like a break? Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.text: Please be seated. Mr. Ostojic, you have all the time of the world, but may I ask you, can you conclude within the next 60 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour? Thank you. Your Honour, we're discussing briefly the allegation that there's a link between the police and Dr. Stakic in this case, and the Office of the Prosecution's theory has quite frankly and in essence been reduced to simply that allegation. And it's Simo Drljaca and the crimes by the police officers in the Municipality of Prijedor that should be somehow attached to Dr. Stakic. The only way that the Office of the Prosecution can meet their burden of proof beyond a reasonable doubt is if they ignore the evidence of the witnesses that the Defence called and the witnesses that the Court called. Those witnesses discussed at length what influence, what authority, what instructions political civilian leaders can give to the police. Both the Defence witnesses as well as the witnesses called by the Court unequivocally, uniformally, and unanimously stated that the civilian political authorities could not and did not in the municipality of the Prijedor in the spring and summer of 1992 control, instruct, order, direct the police. The Office of the Prosecution in their tireless efforts to meet their mandate shows us Exhibit S107A, and they purport in their oral argument that it's a document prepared by Mr. Simo Drljaca on the 31st of May, 1992, where he states in the first paragraph, and with the Court's permission and the usher's assistance, we may place it on the ELMO, I'll begin reading and I'm sure we can all catch up: "With a view to the speedy and efficient establishment of peace on the territory of Prijedor Municipality and in accordance with the decision of the Crisis Staff, I hereby order the following" in the first paragraph. My colleague and learned friend Mr. Lukic spent some time with witnesses trying to establish how could someone who writes this letter, if given authority, why would he do so in a singular form and say "I hereby order" as opposed to "we hereby order." The interesting thing about this document, Your Honour, is that the Office of the Prosecution relies heavily on this document to show that there was some connection between the police and the civilian political authorities. But once again, not surprising, the Office of the Prosecution in a broad manner fails and ignores to discuss the document in its totality completely and thoroughly. Instead, they highlight the first paragraph, but refuse and otherwise ignore to review what Mr. Drljaca writes on paragraph 15 of this critical document of theirs. They talk to you briefly about the issues of knowledge, effective control, substantial participation, but they do not mention in their objective and honest efforts paragraph 15 of Document S107A. Paragraph 15, Mr. Drljaca again in the singular states: "I most strictly prohibit giving any information whatsoever concerning the functioning of this collection centre." He continues to say: "All Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. official documents shall be kept at the collection centre and may be taken out or destroyed only with the permission of the chief of the Prijedor public security station." We can break this document and these sentences down to see what the inferences should be, what the honest and objective, reasonable, logical inferences must be. Does Simo Drljaca here provide any information to the civilian political authorities regarding the atrocities that were occurring at the camps? Of course not. The inference is and the only reasonable inference by virtue of the OTP's document is that it was prohibited and restricted from telling anyone or discussing with anyone the activities in these, as they call them on the third line "collection centres." Does Simo Drljaca in this paragraph 15 of Document 107A state that the documents shall be kept at the Municipal Assembly building? No. To be kept under his control at the "collection centres." Mr. Simo Drljaca says who can take out the documents and who must obtain permission to take out those documents. Can we infer that the civilian political leaders are able to take out documents from this collection centre, detention facility, camp? Or was there truly no one superior to Simo Drljaca in Prijedor in the spring and summer of 1992 which gave him the absolute right to say that only he can authorise it and that only he can decide who can get any such information? Is the reasonable inference that there is a link between the police and the civilian municipal authorities as a result of S107A, or is it honestly fair when you look at this document to state that paragraph 15 simply exonerates the civilian municipal authorities -- and it's clear that any knowledge alleged by the Office of the Prosecution is baseless unless they reconcile reasonably, logically the provisions of paragraph 15 as quoted by Mr. Drljaca on the 31st of May, 1992. The Office of the Prosecution does not address many of critical issues necessary in order to obtain a conviction. Thank you. They do from time to time, as I've stated on several occasions, touch our emotional hearts by talking about the magnitude of killings, by discussing some rather tragic and horrific experiences that occurred in Prijedor. Once again, it's my position that their documents and their arguments are completely and wholeheartedly distorted. When they discuss an issue of such sensitivity as the killing of 200 men at Mount Vlasic, do they address the Court's concern as to whether these killings were natural and foreseeable? Of course not. They argue under the cloth of magnitude of killings that everything was foreseeable and natural. When they talk about the intervention platoon and the request to form an intervention platoon, did they provide any evidence that the intervention platoon was actually formed pursuant to the request? Do they share with the Court that on June 17th, 1992, the task of the request to form an intervention platoon was not, as they allege, to kill innocent Muslims and Croats in Prijedor, the task, the hope was to reduce the level of crime, looting, and theft that was occurring in the municipality. The order, the request of June 17th, 1992, that the intervention platoon be formed clearly and unequivocally states: "The basic task of preventing theft and other criminal activity on the municipal territory." What is the inference? The inference, if you have an extraordinary imagination, as we know the Prosecution does, that with most genocides, the first thing you do is disarm. This, too, according to them is an element that if you form or request that a form to prevent theft and to prevent criminal activity is merely yet another element of a criminal plan, of a joint criminal enterprise that manifested itself over two months after the request to be formed, so from June 17th through August 20th, their theory is that it's that intervention platoon. What they don't give to the Court, what they refuse to give to the Court, what they refuse to give to their experts are the military daily reports which show unequivocally and without doubt that there were numerous groups, individuals who were committing sporadic, random, and uncontrollable acts of violence within the municipality. Not within some common design, not within some joint criminal enterprise, not within a criminal plan. Individuals without any rationale, without any dignity were performing the killings in the Prijedor Municipality. It's convenient for the Office of the Prosecution to twist and to manipulate the facts so that they can distort the truth. However, they should reconcile for us, and I'd like to hear their creative argument, how is it that when you issue a request asking that an intervention platoon be tasked to prevent theft and criminal activity, how does that in any logical or reasonable manner transform itself into being a directive to kill, a directive to commit massacre, a directive to commit atrocities? The Prosecution is persistent in muddying the waters. The next claim in their oral argument, the uniforms are an enormously big issue. Let's show a picture of Dr. Stakic in a uniform. That should strike the Trial Chamber in a negative manner. That should be held against Dr. Stakic. That in and of itself, according to their imagination, is a criminal act. What they don't do is give the Court the honest assessment of that fact. They don't share with the Court the honest view of things as they existed in Prijedor in 1992. If we may have S42, with the Court's permission and the usher's assistance, on the ELMO. S432. While they're putting that on the ELMO, the Office of the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask you once again, please slow down a little bit. I like the French language very much, but unfortunately, it's a little bit longer than the English one. So therefore, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I apologise. Now, the Office of the Prosecution in their clever attempts to highlight some of the evidence told us that the Crisis Staff ordered uniforms. Crisis Staff ordered uniforms. I'm requesting that this Court examine every word that the Office of the Prosecution alleges, every sentence is distorted. All the evidence that they bring forth is distorted. Here we have a document, S432, despite what the Office of the Prosecution says, Crisis Staff ordered uniforms. Second paragraph of that document clearly states "the Prijedor Municipal Assembly acquired a certain quantity of material for sewing flags and green camouflage uniforms," et cetera. Not the Crisis Staff. What importance does that make? What distinction? Does that distinction make any difference in our case? It does when you review in its totality the credibility of that which the Office of the Prosecution is offering. It matters a lot when they misstate purposefully and misconstrue and distort facts in order to cloud the issues, to meet their mandate and goal of a conviction. Also, I'm being reminded that the document references, as I stopped reading it, green camouflage uniforms according to delivery notes 227/92 of 3 May 1992. Clearly, from the evidence that they saw, that they produced, the Crisis Staff was not in existence on the 3rd of May. They want it to be. They need it to be. But they have no proof. The inference, however, and how I view their analysis and attempt to sway this Court does not end here. The distinction is small to say that the Office of the Prosecution is unfair on one hand to suggest that the Crisis Staff ordered uniforms, but in fact it was the Municipal Assembly. However, I believe it's their duty and obligation to share with the Court and to analyse with the Court if not the Defence evidence and the Court's evidence, at least be honest enough with the evidence that they put forth. With respect to uniforms, a young man by the man of Mevludin Sejmenovic testified, he testified over a long period of time. He testified both in direct and cross-examination. He testified that when he was at one of the camps, the journalists were asked who came on the 5th of August if they wanted to interview him. They refused. They did not want to talk to politicians. So he was not interviewed by the British and American press. But we'll analyse that in our briefs in greater detail. Uniforms, does Mr. Sejmenovic address the issue of uniforms? I believe he does. In his testimony, specifically on pages 4.857 ending on page 4.858, he states, on line 20, 4.857: "Q. Okay, before the takeover, when you saw Dr. Stakic in the Assembly or elsewhere, was he wearing -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. did he ever wear a uniform?" Answer by Mr. Sejmenovic, the OTP witness who testified in several cases: "Not usually, no. But I think I did see him in uniform once, but I can't confirm that absolutely because most of the deputies at the last meeting did wear uniforms. We didn't like wearing uniforms, but they said it was wartime and they had been mobilised and that was quite usual." You see, Mr. Sejmenovic as a deputy before April 30th, 1992, acknowledges, admits that he, too, was required to wear a uniform. He, too, wore a uniform and was in attendance at a meeting where uniforms were being worn, green camouflage and the like. It is simply wrong and distorted not to review Mr. Sejmenovic's comments about uniforms in light of their allegation that the uniform is part of a criminal plan, the wearing of a uniform is part of this joint criminal enterprise. The inference from what Mr. Sejmenovic suggests is plain and obvious; the uniform did not and does not matter. It's only a further attempt by the Prosecution, because they weren't given the opportunity to talk about Dr. Stakic's brother, they were not given an opportunity to talk about issues of flight, that they can further cloud and muddy the issues. Next issue, if I may, agenda. The Office of the Prosecution expense an enormous time talking about agenda, how important it is. Did they forget the Court called a witness, that the Court ask Mr. Slavko Budimir about agendas, how they were set, who set them, what the discussions were? Of course they forget. Not intentionally. It was simply an omission, just like with their experts when they omitted to review the totality of the evidence before they present an argument. Just like when we make an argument that as in most genocides, disarming people is the first step to genocide. It was an honest omission. Review the testimony of Mr. Budimir in its totality, and we'll find what weight and credibility the argument that Dr. Stakic may or may not have set the agenda is truly worth being called a criminal plan or an element to satisfy criminal conduct. I must say that I have been somewhat critical of the purported in-house experts by the Office of the Prosecution. We fought very hard and argued very vigorously that a search and seizure of Dr. Stakic after his arrest without a proper chain of custody is a violation of all fundamental rights. We lost, unfortunately, on that issue. If we can have, with the Court's permission, the exhibit that was utilised Friday which had Dr. Stakic's ID card and purportedly, as my learned friend said, his membership card to the SDS. I can't recall the number, and I apologise to the Court. S235-12. Thank you. Now, Your Honour, I've made some rather strong statements, but I think I've backed them up when I say that they distort the evidence and they don't put forth the truth and don't tell the Court what a reasonable inference should be based upon the totality of the evidence. Viewing Exhibit S235-12, if we can just pan out a little to get the entirety of the document, and my objection to Mr. O'Donnell's creative way of performing searches and seizures and reporting pursuant to recognised chain of custody rules, this document is given to the Court to suggest, as Mr. Koumjian of the Office of the Prosecutor states, in English, American English he states, "We call this a card-carrying member of the SDS, even up until the time of his arrest." This case is not about the Serbs; it's about Dr. Stakic. Did they distort this evidence? That's the question I would ask. Are you correct, Defence, that this is not the card-carrying membership of Dr. Stakic? Was Mr. O'Donnell honest when he put forth this exhibit and said that this is his membership card? Did the OTP really believe that this was the membership of Dr. Stakic? Ladies and gentlemen and Your Honours, I have the card that's depicted on this exhibit, the original, and I would ask the usher to please place it upon the ELMO. Now, Your Honour, here's how creative the Office of the Prosecution is.
